metais test — Render every example of a package and compare it with the outputs
it should produce.

Usage:
  metais test [<package>] [--example <name>]... [--update [--dry-run]]
              [--limit <name>=<value>]... [--json]

The package is a source directory, the current directory when omitted, or a
packed package file, whose examples are read in place. The package is opened and
verified whole, and every template is parsed; an error there is reported and no
example runs.

An example is a directory under examples/: inputs/ is a data directory, read as
--data reads one; expected/ is the output directory a render should write;
example.yaml may give a title, a description, and now, the render time. Every
example runs, or each one --example names, in byte order of name, whatever
another found. Its inputs are validated, with findings located in
examples/<name>/inputs/; if they are valid it is rendered in memory as metais
render renders, with now from example.yaml or none, and nothing else of the
host. The package digest a template sees, and the provenance tag's
package_digest, are sha256: and 64 zeros, and the provenance tool is test, so an
expected output records nothing that changes with the package or the tool.

When expected/ exists, its files are compared with the render's by path, byte
for byte; directories are ignored. A file the render did not write is
example.output_missing, one it wrote that expected/ lacks is
example.output_unexpected, and different content is example.output_differs: for
text, a unified diff, of at most 40 lines here and 16 KiB in --json; for a
binary file, the first differing byte and both sizes and digests. Its cause
names the first likely explanation that applies: line endings, one final
newline, a byte order mark, or trailing whitespace. A container output's zip is
compared byte for byte as any file is; its comparison by entries is not yet part
of metais. An example without expected/ is rendered and not compared.

--update, on a source directory only, makes each selected example's expected/
exactly its render: every file that is missing or differs is written, through a
staging directory inside expected/, and every file there the render no longer
writes is removed, with any directory that empties. Only an example whose inputs
validated and that rendered is updated, and nothing outside
examples/<name>/expected/ is ever removed. Each file written or removed is
listed; with --dry-run they are listed and nothing is written.

test exits 1 when any example fails.

Operands:
  <package>
      A source directory, or a packed package file; the current directory when
      omitted. - is refused, since a package is read with random access.

Flags:
  --example <name>
      Test only this example; repeatable. Without it, every example is tested.
      May be given more than once.
  --update
      Make each selected example's expected/ exactly its render, writing and
      removing files there; a source directory only.
  --dry-run
      With --update, list the files it would write and remove, and write
      nothing.
  --limit <name>=<value>
      Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than
      its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.
      May be given more than once.
  --fail-on <severity>
      With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error
      does; no finding's severity changes. Values: error, warning. Default:
      error.
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  Every finding, then a line counting the errors, warnings and notes, then one
  line per example with its status and each difference, a text difference's diff
  beneath it; with --update, each file written or removed. With --json, one
  metais.test/1 document.

  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.

      --dry-run is given without --update.
      Next: metais test <package> --update --dry-run
  usage.not_a_source_directory
      --update is given with a packed package, which is not edited.
      Next: metais test <dir> --update

      Next: metais test <package> --example <name>
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais test --help

Examples:
  metais test
      Tests every example of the source directory in the working directory.
  metais test report-1.0.0.metais --example basic
      Tests the example basic of a packed package.
  metais test --update --dry-run
      Lists what --update would write into and remove from each example's
      expected/.
  metais test --json
      Prints every finding and each example's result as one metais.test/1
      document.
